proof_nl:
Fix an integer n > 1 and let x be a real number with 0 <= x < 1. Set m = floor(n x). Then m is an integer and, by definition of the floor function,

m/n <= x < (m+1)/n.

We compare E(n,x) with E(n,m/n). First, since m/n is rational with n(m/n)=m, we have floor(n(m/n)) = m. So

E(n,m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k.

Now let 1 <= k <= n. Because x >= m/n and the map t -> floor(t) is nondecreasing, we get

floor(kx) >= floor(km/n).

Therefore, term by term,

floor(kx)/k >= floor(km/n)/k.

Summing over k = 1, ..., n gives

sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k >= sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k.

Since floor(nx) = m, it follows that

E(n,x) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k <= m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k = E(n,m/n).

This is exactly the desired inequality.
solver_summary: For x in [0,1), let m=floor(nx), so x lies in [m/n,(m+1)/n). Since x >= m/n and floor is monotone, floor(kx) >= floor(km/n) for each k=1,...,n. Because E(n,x)=m-Σ floor(kx)/k and E(n,m/n)=m-Σ floor(km/n)/k, the inequality follows by termwise comparison.
